sessions.final_text:
I rewrote `parse_amount` in `tally/money.py`, and `12.5` now parses to 1250 cents. The old code took the digits after the decimal point as a plain number of cents, so `12.5` became 12.05. It also applied the sign only to the whole part, so `-0.50` came out wrong.

The new version strips the sign first and applies it to the whole amount. It pads a one-digit fraction to tenths, raises `ValueError` for more than two decimal places, and rejects malformed text. Thousands separators, whole numbers and surrounding spaces still work. `ValueError` is still raised for text that isn't an amount, including cases like `"1."` and `"1.-5"`, and a leading `+` is still accepted. `parse_amount` has only one caller, `csvio.py`, which needed no change.

I added tests to `tests/test_money.py` for tenths, the sign cases, `"1.234"` and malformed input. interlock ran `checks/parse-repro.sh` and the full unit suite on the result, and both passed (23 tests). I recorded claims for all three criteria. `spec` rests on the unit tests I added plus the existing ones, and it still needs the independent verifier.

All three criteria hold on tree 739032e.

- **repro**: pass (observed). interlock ran `checks/parse-repro.sh` on this tree and it printed `ok: 12.5 is 1250 cents`.
- **spec**: pass (tested). My ad hoc script, run alongside the 23 unit tests, gave:
  - `12.5` → 1250, `-0.50` → -50, `-3.25` → -325.
  - `1.234` raises `ValueError`.
  - `1,234.56` → 123456, `7` → 700, `" 7 "` → 700.
  - Malformed text such as `abc`, `5.` and `1.2.3` raises `ValueError`.

  One small behaviour change: non-ASCII digits such as Arabic-Indic ones were accepted before and are now rejected, which I don't count as a gap.
- **regression**: pass (tested). The existing unit suite passes, 23 tests OK.

checks_run: cat tally/money.py; git diff --stat e331edb HEAD; interlock check run --criterion repro 2>&1 | tail -15; interlock check run --criterion regression 2>&1 | tail -8

interlock assess add --criterion repro --strength observed --ref "interlock check run --criterion repro" --note "Check passed on tree 739032e: ok 12.5 is 1250 cents"
interlock assess add --criterion spec --strength tested --ref "python3 /tmp/t.py ad hoc + unit suite (23 OK)" --note "12.5->1250, -0.50->-50, -3.25->-325, 1.234 VE, 1,234.56->123456, 7->700, spaces ok, malformed VE. Minor: non-ASCII digits (e.g. Arabic-Indic) formerly accepted by int(), now rejected; not an amount per goal."
interlock assess add --criterion regression --strength tested --ref "interlock check run --criterion regression" --note "Unit suite passes, 23 tests OK"
ls tests; cat checks/parse-repro.sh; grep -rn parse_amount --include=*.py . | grep -v "^./tests"

python3 - <<'E'
p='tests/test_money.py'
s=open(p).read()
add='''    def test_one_decimal_digit_is_tenths(self):
        self.assertEqual(parse_amount("12.5"), 1250)

    def test_sign_covers_fraction(self):
        self.assertEqual(parse_amount("-0.50"), -50)
        self.assertEqual(parse_amount("-3.25"), -325)

    def test_too_many_decimals(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            parse_amount("1.234")

    def test_malformed(self):
        for bad in ("", "abc", "1.", "1.-5", "--1", "1.2.3"):
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                parse_amount(bad)

'''
s=s.replace('class FormatCentsTest',add.rstrip('\n')+'\n\n\nclass FormatCentsTest',1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
E
sed -n 1,20p tally/money.py; sh checks/parse-repro.sh; python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -q 2>&1|tail -5
interlock check run --criterion repro; interlock check run --criterion regression

interlock claim add --criterion repro --strength observed --tree auto --ref "interlock check run --criterion repro" --note "check passes on output tree: 12.5 -> 1250"
interlock claim add --criterion regression --strength tested --tree auto --ref "interlock check run --criterion regression" --note "23 tests pass incl. new tenths, sign, >2 decimals, malformed cases"
interlock claim add --criterion spec --strength tested --tree auto --ref "python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -q" --note "new unit tests cover tenths, -0.50, -3.25, 1.234 ValueError; existing tests cover separators, whole numbers, spaces"
